### `identity.bad_id`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
An id breaks [a-z][a-z0-9_]* or is longer than 48 bytes. The hint gives the repaired id:
lower-cased, each invalid character replaced by _, x in front if it does not start with a letter.
To fix: Write the repaired id.
Bad:   [feature.Mill-A]
Fixed: [feature.mill_a]
```

### `identity.bad_key`

error, milestone 2, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A step returned a key that breaks 2.2, or an unknown class; says which rule.
To fix: The repaired key, as for bad_id, or the class list.
Bad:   step.out.feature("Pool 1", ...)
Fixed: step.out.feature("pool_1", ...)
```

### `identity.clear_empty`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A clear removed nothing: no instance of the producers in its by stands inside it. The record
gives the nearest instance of a by producer and its distance.
To fix: Move the clear onto the instance meant, or delete it if it is no longer wanted.
Bad:   [clear.a]
       at = [10, 10]
       radius = 2
       by = ["s"]   (nearest instance of s at 6 m)
Fixed: [clear.a]
       at = [10, 10]
       radius = 7
       by = ["s"]
```

### `identity.duplicate_id`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
Two tables in one namespace share an id, in one file or across layers. The record names both.
To fix: Rename one, or merge them in one layer.
Bad:   [feature.a]  in world.toml   and   [feature.a]  in layers/b.toml
Fixed: [feature.a]  and  [feature.a2]
```

### `identity.key_collision`

error, milestone 2, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
One step gave two things one key; names both positions.
To fix: Build the key from place, with the SDK's naming calls.
Bad:   step.out.feature("pool", ...) twice
Fixed: step.out.feature(f"pool_{i}_{j}", ...)   (a key from its place)
```

### `identity.key_in_text`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A produced name (one holding #) is written in a key that takes a name. Produced names belong to
the engine and may change between builds; text selects produced things by place instead. The
hint gives the { of, class, near } form at the thing's current position.
To fix: Write the { of, class, near } form the hint gives.
Bad:   on = { ref = "s#e12" }
Fixed: on = { of = "s", class = "edge", near = [40, 12] }
```

### `identity.lock_asset_missing`

error, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A recorded item's asset is no longer bound by the pack.
To fix: Bind the asset again, or re-record with via lock.
Bad:   [asset.oak_old] removed from the pack; locks/old_grove.toml records asset = "oak_old"
Fixed: bind oak_old again, or run: via lock world.toml old_grove
```

### `identity.lock_differs`

info, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
What the producers would now do inside a lock, and live names dropped for a recorded one, as counts.
To fix: Re-record with via lock, or leave it.
Bad:   [scatter.oaks] density 0.6 -> 0.3 with [lock.old_grove] recorded at 0.6
Fixed: via lock world.toml old_grove   (or leave the record as it is)
```

### `identity.lock_ground_moved`

warning, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
Recorded items stand on ground that moved; count and largest change.
To fix: Re-record with via lock, or edit the ground's cause.
Bad:   [feature.hill] raised 2 m under [lock.old_grove]
Fixed: via lock world.toml old_grove   (or move the hill back)
```

### `identity.lock_pin_clash`

error, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A recorded item overlaps a pin; names both.
To fix: Move the pin, or re-record with via lock.
Bad:   [pin.oak] at = [60, 132]   (a recorded item of old_grove stands there)
Fixed: [pin.oak] at = [70, 132]
```

### `identity.lock_rerecorded`

info, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A record was replaced; counts of the difference.
To fix: None needed; review the record's diff.
Bad:   via lock world.toml old_grove   (a second time, after a change)
Fixed: nothing to change: read the counts, then review locks/old_grove.toml's diff
```

### `identity.lock_unrecorded`

error, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A lock has no record.
To fix: via lock <world> <id>.
Bad:   [lock.old_grove] region = [...], by = ["oaks"]   (no locks/old_grove.toml)
Fixed: via lock world.toml old_grove
```

### `identity.near_none`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A selection asks a maker for a class it has no candidate of, so it resolves to nothing. Said once
per maker and class, listing every selection left with nothing; the record gives the nearest
candidate of any class and its distance, or says the maker made nothing.
To fix: Ask for a class the maker produces, or select another maker.
Bad:   on = { of = "s", class = "area", near = [10, 10] }   (s made no areas)
Fixed: on = { of = "s", class = "edge", near = [10, 10] }
```

### `identity.no_place`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A selection's class is field or row. Fields and rows cover the world and have no place to be
nearest to.
To fix: Read a field by name or 'tag:<tag>' in a formula; select a feature or instance by place.
Bad:   on = { of = "s", class = "field", near = [0, 0] }
Fixed: value = "= f('tag:b')"
```

### `identity.no_previous`

info, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
There is no baseline build to report changes against, so this build's change report is empty.
Information only; the next build has one.
To fix: None needed; to compare with a given build now, pass --against.
Bad:   via build world.toml --out build/new   (first build there)
Fixed: via build world.toml --out build/new --against build/a
```

### `identity.not_a_producer`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
`by` names a set, or a maker that places no instances (a network, a cells table, a where
feature). A pin or clear acts on the instances of producers only.
To fix: Name the producers that place on it.
Bad:   by = ["n"]   (n is a network)
Fixed: by = ["s"]   (s a scatter within n's areas)
```

### `identity.of_ambiguous`

error, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
of names a maker with several classes and no class.
To fix: The classes, with a count of each near near.
Bad:   on = { of = "town", near = [120, 80] }   (town makes areas and cells)
Fixed: on = { of = "town", class = "cell", near = [120, 80] }
```

### `identity.on_both`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
`on` has both `ref` and `of`. ref names an authored thing by id; of names a maker whose produced
thing is selected by place. One on uses one.
To fix: Keep ref for an authored thing, of for a produced one.
Bad:   on = { ref = "a", of = "s", class = "edge", near = [0, 0] }
Fixed: on = { ref = "a", t = 0.5 }
```

### `identity.pin_in_clear`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A pin stands inside a clear. The pin stays: hand edits never remove each other. The record names
both.
To fix: Leave it if the pin is what the spot is for; otherwise move the pin or the clear.
Bad:   [pin.a] at = [10, 10]   and   [clear.b] at = [10, 10], radius = 4
Fixed: [pin.a] at = [20, 10]
```

### `identity.pin_in_keep_out`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A pin stands where a keep_out field is above 0. A pin is placed where it is written, so it stays;
the record names the field.
To fix: Move the pin, or accept it there.
Bad:   [pin.a]  at = [10, 10]   (keep_out 1 there)
Fixed: [pin.a]  at = [30, 10]
```

### `identity.pin_overlap`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A pin overlaps an instance of a producer that is not in its by, so that instance was not removed
for it. The record names both.
To fix: Add that producer to by, or move the pin.
Bad:   by = ["s"]   (overlaps an instance of t)
Fixed: by = ["s", "t"]
```

### `identity.pin_removed`

info, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
What a pin removed: the instances of its by producers that its footprint overlapped on its own
level (what stands on another surface over or under it stays), with count and names. Information
only.
To fix: Nothing if intended; narrow by to keep them.
Bad:   by = ["s", "t"]   (removed instances of t that should stay)
Fixed: by = ["s"]
```

### `identity.pins_overlap`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
Two pins' footprints overlap. Pins are placed exactly as written, so neither can give way. The
record names both and the overlap's size.
To fix: Move one by at least the overlap's size.
Bad:   [pin.a] at = [10, 10]   and   [pin.b] at = [11, 10]
Fixed: [pin.a] at = [10, 10]   and   [pin.b] at = [14, 10]
```

### `identity.reselected`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A selection resolved to a different produced name than in the baseline: the thing near its near
point changed (an edge was cut, say). A run diagnostic; the record names both and the distance
moved.
To fix: Move near onto the thing meant, or select a feature that does not split (section 3).
Bad:   on = { of = "n", class = "edge", near = [50, 1] }   (now nearer a new edge)
Fixed: on = { ref = "a", t = 0.5 }   (a the path the edge came from)
```

### `identity.reserved`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
An id is world, an import id is a collection's name (feature, field, step and the like), or a
mount, set item or kind surface is named start, end or ground. Those names are taken by the
language.
To fix: Choose another name; the hint gives the nearest free one.
Bad:   [feature.world]
Fixed: [feature.world_a]
```

### `identity.unknown_lock`

error, milestone 3, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
via lock was given an id that is no lock.
To fix: The nearest lock id.
Bad:   via lock world.toml old_grov
Fixed: via lock world.toml old_grove
```

### `identity.unknown_maker`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
`of` names no maker. `data.nearest` holds the nearest maker id.
To fix: Write the id of a maker the world declares.
Bad:   on = { of = "sx", class = "edge", near = [0, 0] }
Fixed: on = { of = "s", class = "edge", near = [0, 0] }
```

### `identity.unknown_place`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
A part of a place name names nothing. `data.nearest` holds the nearest match.
To fix: Write the place name as declared.
Bad:   at = "a.ned"
Fixed: at = "a.end"
```

### `identity.unknown_producer`

error, milestone 1, `spec/identity.md`.

```text
`by` names no producer. `data.nearest` holds the nearest producer id.
To fix: Write the id of a producer the world declares.
Bad:   by = ["sx"]
Fixed: by = ["s"]
```

## import

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `import.binding_differs` | error | 4 | `id` | One asset id or material name bound differently by two packs of the build; `data.id`. (M4) |
| `import.coarser` | info | 4 | `ratio` | The parent's posts are coarser than the import's, so detail is lost; `data.ratio`. (M4) |
| `import.cycle` | error | 4 |  | Worlds that import each other; the files of the loop, in order. (M4) |
| `import.datum_differs` | error | 4 | `datum`, `parent_datum` | The import and the parent declare different datums and the import has no `lift`; `data.datum`, `data.parent_datum`. (M4) |
| `import.exit_mismatch` | error | 4 | `attribute`, `exit_value`, `answer_value`, `write` | An answer to an exit whose attribute differs from the exit's; `data.attribute`, `data.exit_value`, `data.answer_value`, the fixing line in `data.write`. (M4) |
| `import.exit_outside` | error | 4 |  | An exit lies outside its import's footprint. (M4) |
| `import.exit_unanswered` | error | 4 | `write` | An exit of a direct import that no parent reference names; the line that answers it in `data.write`. (M4) |
| `import.field_differs` | error | 4 | `field` | An import's field and the parent's field of one name differ in role, type or unit; `data.field`. (M4) |
| `import.field_unmatched` | warning | 4 | `field`, `write` | An import's field the parent does not declare, so not brought; `data.field`, the declaration in `data.write`. (M4) |
| `import.give_outside` | error | 4 | `area` | A given field does not cover the fill's extent as placed; `data.area`. (M4) |
| `import.given_dropped` | warning | 4 | `attribute` | A given feature's attribute the fill's kind does not declare was dropped; `data.attribute`. (M4) |
| `import.given_type` | error | 4 | `accepts` | What is given is not the form the given `accepts`; `data.accepts`. (M4) |
| `import.given_unknown` | error | 4 | `nearest` | `give` names a name the import does not declare in `[given]`; the nearest name. (M4) |
| `import.lift_on_datum` | error | 4 |  | `lift` on an import that declares the parent's datum. (M4) |
| `import.no_datum` | warning | 4 | `write`, `lift_hint` | The import or the parent declares no datum and the import has no `lift`; the line to add in `data.write`, and `data.lift_hint` the lift that meets this world's ground across the edge (5). (M4) |
| `import.outside` | warning | 4 | `area` | Part of an import's footprint lies past the parent's extent and is not brought; `data.area`. (M4) |
| `import.overlap` | warning | 4 | `area` | Two imports' footprints, as placed, intersect with an area above 0; `data.area` (6.8). (M4) |
| `import.place_blended` | warning | 4 | `weight`, `moved` | A place the parent names stands where the import's weight is below 1; `data.weight`, `data.moved`. (M4) |
| `import.seam` | warning | 4 | `grade`, `lift_hint` | A step in the ground across the join steeper than `max_grade`, worst first by data.grade; `data.lift_hint` the lift that meets this world's ground across the edge (5). (M4) |
| `import.surface_dropped` | warning | 7 | `surface` | A kind surface of an import leaves the lattice where the import is placed and is not brought; `data.surface` (6.1). (M7) |

### `import.binding_differs`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
Two worlds of one build, a parent and an import or two imports, each resolve asset ids with their
own pack, and those packs bind one asset id or material name to different things. A build holds
one binding per name, so neither may win silently. `data.id` holds the name; the record names
both packs.
To fix: Bind the name the same way in both packs, or rename it in one of them.
Bad:   parent pack: [asset.a] primitive = "box", size = [2, 2, 2]
       import pack: [asset.a] primitive = "box", size = [1, 1, 1]
Fixed: import pack: [asset.a_small] primitive = "box", size = [1, 1, 1]
```

### `import.coarser`

info, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The parent's post spacing is coarser than the import's, so the import's fields are read at fewer
points than it was built at and its finer detail is not carried. `data.ratio` holds the parent's
spacing over the import's. No filter is applied.
To fix: Nothing, if the detail does not matter; otherwise give the parent a finer resolution.
Bad:   resolution = 2        (the import's is 1)
Fixed: resolution = 1
```

### `import.cycle`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
A world imports a world that, directly or through others, imports it back. A world built apart
must build alone, so a loop has no first world. The record names the files of the loop in order.
One file imported at two places in the tree is not a loop.
To fix: Remove the import that closes the loop.
Bad:   a/world.toml: [import.p] file = "../world.toml"
Fixed: remove [import.p] from a/world.toml
```

### `import.datum_differs`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The import's world and the parent each name what their height zero is, and the names differ, so
the import's heights mean something else in the parent. `data.datum` and `data.parent_datum` hold
the two names.
To fix: Give the import a lift, the metres between the two zeros, or make both datums one.
Bad:   [import.a]           (a: datum = "b"; parent: datum = "c")
       file = "a/world.toml"
Fixed: [import.a]
       file = "a/world.toml"
       lift = 2
```

### `import.exit_mismatch`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
An exit's kind lists attributes in `exit = [...]` that an answer must match, and a parent feature
that answers the exit has another value for one of them, or none. `data.attribute` names it;
`data.exit_value` and `data.answer_value` hold both values; `data.write` holds the line that makes
the answer match.
To fix: Write the line in data.write on the answering feature, or answer with a feature whose
kind declares the attribute.
Bad:   ends_at = "a.e"
       width   = 4        (the exit a.e has width = 6)
Fixed: ends_at = "a.e"
       width   = 6
```

### `import.exit_outside`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
An exit of an import lies outside the footprint the parent brings, so it would leave from ground
that is not in the parent.
To fix: Widen the footprint to hold the exit, or move the exit inside it in the import.
Bad:   footprint = [[0, 0], [4, 0], [4, 8], [0, 8]]     (the exit stands at [7, 4])
Fixed: footprint = [[0, 0], [8, 0], [8, 8], [0, 8]]
```

### `import.exit_unanswered`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
An import declares an exit, a place where something leaves it, and nothing in the parent names
it. The parent owns the region around the import and must say what happens there: something that
goes on, or a deliberate end. `data.write` holds the line that answers it.
To fix: End a path there with the line in data.write, or place a feature on it that ends it.
Bad:   [import.a]            (a declares the exit e)
       file = "a/world.toml"
Fixed: [feature.p]
       path    = [[0, 4]]
       ends_at = "a.e"
```

### `import.field_differs`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The import and the parent each declare a field of one name, and its role, type or unit differs,
so the import's values cannot stand in the parent's field. `data.field` names it; the record
gives both declarations.
To fix: Declare the field alike in both worlds, or rename it in one.
Bad:   parent: [field.m] role = "keep_out"      import: [field.m] (no role)
Fixed: import: [field.m] role = "keep_out"
```

### `import.field_unmatched`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The import has a field that the parent does not declare, so nothing of it reaches the parent's
build. `data.field` names it; `data.write` holds the declaration that brings it.
To fix: Declare the field in the parent, as data.write gives, or leave it out on purpose.
Bad:   (the import declares [field.m]; the parent does not)
Fixed: [field.m]
       base = 0
```

### `import.give_outside`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
A parent gives a fill a field, and part of the fill's extent, as placed, lies past the parent's
extent, where the parent's field has no value. `data.area` holds that area in square metres.
To fix: Place the fill inside the parent's extent, or widen the parent's extent.
Bad:   at = [28, 0]        (an 8 m fill in a parent 32 m wide)
Fixed: at = [24, 0]
```

### `import.given_dropped`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
A parent gives a fill features, which take the kind the fill's [given] names. One of them has an
attribute that kind does not declare, so the fill does not see it. `data.attribute` names it.
To fix: Declare the attribute in the fill's kind, or leave it off the parent's features.
Bad:   [given.g] kind = "k"     (k declares no attribute c; the parent's feature writes c)
Fixed: [kind.k.defaults]
       c = 0
```

### `import.given_type`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
A parent gives a fill something of another form than the fill's [given] accepts: a field where it
accepts a region, a region where it accepts features. `data.accepts` holds the form it accepts.
To fix: Give a thing of that form.
Bad:   give = { g = "r" }      (g accepts a field; r is a region)
Fixed: give = { g = "h" }      (h is a field)
```

### `import.given_unknown`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
A parent's give hands down a name that the import does not declare in a [given] table, so nothing
in it would read what is given. `data.nearest` holds the nearest declared name.
To fix: Use a name the import declares, or declare it in the import.
Bad:   give = { lnad = "h" }
Fixed: give = { land = "h" }
```

### `import.lift_on_datum`

error, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The import and the parent name the same datum, so their heights already share a zero, and a lift
would move the import off it.
To fix: Remove the lift; or, if the import's zero is really another, name its own datum.
Bad:   [import.a]            (both worlds: datum = "b")
       lift = 2
Fixed: [import.a]
       file = "a/world.toml"
```

### `import.no_datum`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The import or the parent does not name what its height zero is, and the import has no lift, so
nothing says the two zeros agree. Heights are taken as they are. `data.write` holds the line to
add; `data.lift_hint` the lift that meets this world's ground across the import's edge (the
median step there), when the edge crosses this world's posts.
To fix: Name one datum in both world files, or give the import a lift (the hint names one).
Bad:   (no datum in either world file)
Fixed: datum = "b"           (in both world files)
```

### `import.outside`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
Part of an import's footprint, as placed, lies past the parent's extent. That part is not brought:
no field values, no instances. `data.area` holds its area in square metres.
To fix: Move the import inside the extent, cut its footprint, or widen the parent's extent.
Bad:   at = [28, 0]        (an 8 m import in a parent 32 m wide)
Fixed: at = [24, 0]
```

### `import.overlap`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
Two imports' footprints, as placed, overlap, so both bring ground to the same posts and the order
of their entries decides it, which nobody chose. `data.area` holds the overlap in square metres.
To fix: Move one, or cut one's footprint so they meet without overlapping.
Bad:   [import.a] at = [0, 0]      [import.b] at = [6, 0]     (both 8 m wide)
Fixed: [import.b] at = [8, 0]
```

### `import.place_blended`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
The parent names a place inside an import, and the import's blend weight there is below 1, so the
place stands on ground the import did not make. `data.weight` holds the weight; `data.moved` the
height difference from the import's own ground.
A path's end named on a place inside the import's footprint is held (composition.md 6.7), so this
is a place outside it, or a place named by a view, which holds nothing. Weight 0 means the place
lies outside the footprint (a place on its edge is inside, within a millimetre once turned).
To fix: Make the blend reach 1 at the place, or move the place further inside the import; for a
weight of 0, end the path on a place inside the footprint, a metre in from its edge.
Bad:   blend = "= smoothstep(0, 4, d)"     (the named place is 1 m inside the edge)
Fixed: blend = "= smoothstep(0, 1, d)"
```

### `import.seam`

warning, milestone 4, `spec/composition.md`, worst first by `data.grade`.

```text
Across the edge of an import's ground, two neighbouring posts of the surface differ by more than
the import's max_grade allows, rise over run. Nothing anchored owns that ground. `data.grade`
holds the steepest; the position is its post inside the footprint. `data.lift_hint` is the lift
that meets this world's ground across the edge (the median step).
To fix: Write a blend that fades over the edge, place an anchored feature that owns the join, set
the lift the hint names when the whole import stands off, or raise max_grade if the step is meant.
Bad:   [import.a]            (its ground stands 4 m above the parent's at its edge)
       file = "a/world.toml"
Fixed: [import.a]
       file  = "a/world.toml"
       blend = "= smoothstep(0, 8, d)"
```

### `import.surface_dropped`

warning, milestone 7, `spec/composition.md`.

```text
An import's kind surfaces come with their features (composition.md 6.1), taken point by point
through the import's frame. A point of this one lands past the lattice (numbers.md 3) where the
import is placed, so the surface is not brought: no mesh, no cut, nothing stands on it.
`data.surface` holds its scoped name.
To fix: Place the import nearer the lattice's middle, or keep the surface inside the import.
Bad:   at = [2147480, 0]     (a surface 7 m long inside the import)
Fixed: at = [2147000, 0]
```

## load

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load.bad_file` | error | 1 |  | An array file's header, size or shape is wrong, or a listed file is missing. |
| `load.bad_target` | warning | 1 |  | An output feature's camera target (a name attribute) is missing, is not the resolved form `{ "at", "name" }` of 9.1, or lies within 1 mm of the eye in plan, or its eye height is missing or not a finite number (15.1); names the feature and the attribute. That feature gets no camera. Hint: check that its kind lists the attribute in `names` (`authority.md` 1.2) and gives the eye height a default. |
| `load.fields_not_drawn` | info | 1 |  | The fields the loader neither drew nor kept, by name. |
| `load.format` | error | 1 |  | A loader found no manifest, or a `format` it does not read; names `diagnostics.json` when present. |
| `load.too_many_materials` | warning | 1 |  | A chunk names more materials than this loader draws; names the chunk and its materials (`fields.md` 7.1). |

### `load.bad_file`

error, milestone 1, `spec/build.md`, covered by the reader tests.

```text
A loader found an array file whose header, size or shape is wrong, or a listed file missing. The
build directory was changed or damaged after the build.
To fix: Run via check on the folder, and build again into a new folder.
Bad:   a build folder copied without its fields folder
Fixed: the whole folder copied
```

### `load.bad_target`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/build.md`, covered by the reader tests.

```text
An output feature's camera target (a name attribute) is missing, not the resolved form
{ "at", "name" }, or within 1 mm of the eye in plan, or its eye height is missing or not a
finite number. That feature gets no camera; no default is guessed.
To fix: Check that the kind lists the attribute in names and gives the eye height a default.
Bad:   [kind.k]
       requires = ["toward"]
Fixed: [kind.k]
       requires = ["toward"]
       names = ["toward"]
       defaults = { eye_height = 1.7 }
```

### `load.fields_not_drawn`

info, milestone 1, `spec/build.md`, covered by the reader tests.

```text
The fields the loader neither drew nor kept, by name. Information only: every field is in the
build; the loader keeps the ones it is told to.
To fix: Nothing; to keep a field, name it in the loader's fields option.
Bad:   fields = []   (a field wanted in the engine)
Fixed: fields = ["b"]
```

### `load.format`

error, milestone 1, `spec/build.md`, covered by the reader tests.

```text
A loader found no manifest.json, or a format it does not read. It names diagnostics.json when
present, since a failed build leaves no manifest.
To fix: Fix the build's errors (see diagnostics.json) and build again, or update the loader.
Bad:   loading a folder where the build failed
Fixed: loading the folder after a build that exits 0
```

### `load.too_many_materials`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/build.md`, covered by the reader tests.

```text
A chunk names more materials than this loader draws at once. The record names the chunk and its
materials.
To fix: Paint fewer materials where they meet, or use a loader that draws more.
Bad:   six materials painted in one chunk
Fixed: four materials there
```

## num

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `num.empty_reduction` | error | 1 |  | A mean, minimum or maximum over a feature with no samples. Names the feature. |
| `num.extent_empty` | error | 1 |  | `extent` has `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0`. Any other wrong form is `doc.type`. |
| `num.extent_not_multiple` | error | 1 |  | The extent's width or height is not a whole multiple of `resolution`. The hint keeps `x0`, `y0` and gives `x1`, `y1` rounded down and up, and the nearest resolutions that divide both widths. |
| `num.not_finite` | error | 1 |  | A number in text is `inf` or `nan`. |
| `num.not_finite_result` | error | 1 |  | A step or a stored feature value would store an infinite or NaN value. Names the step or feature and the row or position. A formula's is `formula.not_finite`. |
| `num.out_of_range` | error | 1 |  | A number in text out of range: a length beyond plus or minus `2^31 - 1` mm, a facing beyond 64 bits, a double whose nearest value is infinite. Computed positions out of range are `geom.range`. |
| `num.overflow` | error | 1 |  | A checked integer operation overflowed. Names the subject and the position. |
| `num.resolution` | error | 1 |  | `resolution` is below 1 mm. |
| `num.seed_range` | error | 1 |  | The world `seed` is negative. |
| `num.seed_type` | error | 1 |  | A seed of the wrong form: a world seed not an integer; a scatter seed not a name, or a name that breaks the id grammar. The hint suggests a name, or the lower-cased form. |
| `num.too_many_posts` | error | 1 |  | `nx * ny` exceeds the post limit. Names `nx`, `ny` and the limit. |
| `num.too_precise` | error | 1 |  | A length is not a whole number of millimetres, or a facing not a whole number of millidegrees. The hint names the two nearest values that are. |

### `num.empty_reduction`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A mean, minimum or maximum was taken over a feature with no samples (no post inside it), so it
has no value. The record names the feature.
To fix: Make the feature large enough to hold a post, or use a finer resolution.
Bad:   value = "= under('mean')"   (a region smaller than one post spacing)
Fixed: the same region with a side of at least 2 post spacings
```

### `num.extent_empty`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
The extent has x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0, so the world has no area.
To fix: Write the corners as [x0, y0, x1, y1] with x1 > x0 and y1 > y0.
Bad:   extent = [100, 0, 0, 100]
Fixed: extent = [0, 0, 100, 100]
```

### `num.extent_not_multiple`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
The extent's width or height is not a whole multiple of the resolution. The hint keeps x0 and y0
and gives x1 and y1 rounded down and up, and the nearest resolutions that divide both widths.
To fix: Write one of them.
Bad:   extent = [0, 0, 100.25, 100]   with resolution = 0.5
Fixed: extent = [0, 0, 100.5, 100]
```

### `num.not_finite`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A number in the text is inf or nan, which no key takes.
To fix: Write a finite number.
Bad:   value = nan
Fixed: value = 0
```

### `num.not_finite_result`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A step or a stored feature value would store an infinite or NaN value. The record names the step
or feature and the row or position. A formula's is formula.not_finite.
To fix: Change the step or value so it yields a finite number there.
Bad:   a step returning a row with value inf
Fixed: the step clamping its result to a finite range
```

### `num.out_of_range`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A number is out of range: a length beyond plus or minus 2^31 - 1 mm, a facing beyond 64 bits, a
double too large to hold.
To fix: Write a number in range.
Bad:   width = 3000000
Fixed: width = 3000
```

### `num.overflow`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`, covered by the workspace tests.

```text
A checked integer operation overflowed (a sum of millimetres, a count). The record names the
subject and the position.
To fix: Bring the values involved into a smaller range: shorter lengths, fewer things.
Bad:   a path whose summed length passes 2^31 - 1 mm
Fixed: the same path split in two
```

### `num.resolution`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
The resolution is below 1 mm.
To fix: Write a post spacing of at least 0.001.
Bad:   resolution = 0.0001
Fixed: resolution = 0.5
```

### `num.seed_range`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
The world seed is negative.
To fix: Write a seed of 0 or more.
Bad:   seed = -1
Fixed: seed = 1
```

### `num.seed_type`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A seed has the wrong form: a world seed that is not an integer, or a scatter seed that is not a
name or breaks the id grammar.
To fix: Write the form the hint suggests.
Bad:   seed = "Base"   (on a scatter)
Fixed: seed = "base"
```

### `num.too_many_posts`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
The grid would hold more posts than the limit; the record names nx, ny and the limit.
To fix: Use a coarser resolution or a smaller extent.
Bad:   extent = [0, 0, 100000, 100000]   with resolution = 0.5
Fixed: extent = [0, 0, 100000, 100000]   with resolution = 8
```

### `num.too_precise`

error, milestone 1, `spec/numbers.md`.

```text
A length is not a whole number of millimetres, or a facing not a whole number of millidegrees.
The hint gives the two nearest values that are.
To fix: Write one of them.
Bad:   width = 1.0005
Fixed: width = 1.001
```

## pack

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pack.accept_refused` | error | 2 |  | `via pack accept` found errors; nothing written. |
| `pack.bad_axes` | error | 1 |  | `front` or `up` is not one of the six signed axes, or both name one axis. |
| `pack.bad_facts` | error | 2 |  | The facts file is not readable, or not in 4.1's form. |
| `pack.bad_model` | error | 2 |  | A model is not readable glTF 2.0, holds a non-finite number or a bad index count, or uses an extension v0 does not read. |
| `pack.material_repeat` | error | 1 |  | A material has `file` without `repeat`, or `repeat` without `file`. |
| `pack.missing_file` | error | 1 | `nearest` | `root`, a file the pack names, or a URI a model references, does not exist. M1 checks `root` and a material's `file`; M2 adds models, `detail` copies and their URIs. |
| `pack.not_found` | error | 1 | `nearest` | The `pack` string names no file; the roots searched, by place. |
| `pack.outside_root` | error | 2 |  | A file reached outside `root`: an absolute URI, a `..` out of it, a scheme other than `data:`, a symbolic link. |
| `pack.range` | error | 1 |  | A pack number out of range: `size` or `repeat` not above 0, `triangles`, `max_relief` below 0, a `colour` part outside 0 to 1. |
| `pack.shadowed` | info | 1 |  | A pack name found in several roots. |
| `pack.stale_facts` | info | 2 |  | The facts file holds ids the pack no longer has. |
| `pack.unaccepted` | info | 2 |  | The pack has model assets and no facts file; revisions cannot be reported. |
| `pack.unknown_material` | error | 1 | `nearest` | A `paint` names a material the pack lacks. |
| `pack.unknown_taxon` | error | 1 | `nearest` | An asset's `taxon`, a selection or a `--taxon` filter names an undeclared taxon. |

### `pack.accept_refused`

error, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
via pack accept found errors; nothing written.
To fix: Fix the listed errors, then accept again.
Bad:   via pack accept PACK with a broken oak.glb
Fixed: oak.glb repaired, then via pack accept PACK
```

### `pack.bad_axes`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
`front` or `up` is not one of the six signed axis names (+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z), or both name
the same axis, so the model's orientation is not fixed.
To fix: Name two different axes, for example front = "-y", up = "+z".
Bad:   front = "+z"
       up    = "-z"
Fixed: front = "-y"
       up    = "+z"
```

### `pack.bad_facts`

error, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
The facts file is not readable, or not in 4.1's form.
To fix: Delete it and run via pack accept PACK.
Bad:   starter.facts.toml edited by hand
Fixed: the file deleted, then via pack accept PACK
```

### `pack.bad_model`

error, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A model is not readable glTF 2.0, holds a non-finite number or a bad index count, or uses an extension v0 does not read.
To fix: Re-export without the named extension, or fix the pointed part.
Bad:   oak.glb using KHR_draco_mesh_compression
Fixed: oak.glb exported without compression
```

### `pack.material_repeat`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A material has `file` without `repeat`, or `repeat` without `file`. A texture needs the length it
repeats over, and a repeat means nothing without a texture.
To fix: Write both keys, or neither (a plain colour).
Bad:   [material.a]
       file = "a.png"
Fixed: [material.a]
       file = "a.png"
       repeat = 2
```

### `pack.missing_file`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A path the pack names does not exist: its `root`, or a material's `file` (in M1; models and their
references are checked from M2). `data.nearest` holds the nearest file name in that folder.
To fix: Correct the path, relative to the pack's root, or add the file.
Bad:   file = "textures/gras.png"
Fixed: file = "textures/grass.png"
```

### `pack.not_found`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
The world's `pack` names no pack file in any pack root. The record lists the roots searched, by
place. `data.nearest` holds the nearest pack name.
To fix: Write the pack name the hint gives, or a relative path to the pack file.
Bad:   pack = "primitve"
Fixed: pack = "primitive"
```

### `pack.outside_root`

error, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A file reached outside root: an absolute URI, a .. out of it, a scheme other than data:, a symbolic link.
To fix: Move the file under root, or move root.
Bad:   file = "../shared/oak.glb"
Fixed: oak.glb moved under root, file = "oak.glb"
```

### `pack.range`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A number in the pack is outside its range: `size` or `repeat` not above 0, `triangles` or
`max_relief` below 0, or a `colour` part outside 0 to 1.
To fix: Write a value inside the range the record gives.
Bad:   colour = [0.4, 1.2, 0.3]
Fixed: colour = [0.4, 1.0, 0.3]
```

### `pack.shadowed`

info, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
The pack name is found in more than one pack root. The first root in search order is used; the
record names it.
To fix: Nothing if the one used is right; otherwise write a relative path to the file meant.
Bad:   pack = "a"   (found in two roots)
Fixed: pack = "packs/a.toml"
```

### `pack.stale_facts`

info, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
The facts file holds ids the pack no longer has.
To fix: Run via pack accept PACK to drop them.
Bad:   [asset.old_oak] removed from the pack, still in the facts file
Fixed: via pack accept PACK
```

### `pack.unaccepted`

info, milestone 2, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
The pack has model assets and no facts file; revisions cannot be reported.
To fix: Run via pack accept PACK.
Bad:   a pack of model assets with no facts file
Fixed: via pack accept PACK
```

### `pack.unknown_material`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
A `paint` names a material that the pack does not declare. `data.nearest` holds the nearest
material name.
To fix: Paint a material the pack declares, or add [material.<name>] to the pack.
Bad:   paint = "gras"
Fixed: paint = "grass"
```

### `pack.unknown_taxon`

error, milestone 1, `spec/assets.md`.

```text
An asset's `taxon`, a selection (`@path`) or a `--taxon` filter names a taxon the pack does not
declare. `data.nearest` holds the nearest declared path.
To fix: Write a declared taxon path, or declare it with [taxon."<path>"].
Bad:   taxon = "prop/bx"
Fixed: taxon = "prop/box"
```

## place

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `place.asset_or_set` | error | 1 |  | A placement writes both `asset` and `set`, or neither; a run writes more than one of `asset`, `set` and `assets`, or none. |
| `place.crowded` | warning | 1 |  | Two produced instances overlap (8.1), one overlaps a thing in a higher layer, or two things one step returned overlap, a member of its run and its instance or two of its instances; names both. |
| `place.gave_way` | info | 1 |  | A producer's candidates dropped by overlap and by relief, as counts, with their box. |
| `place.keep_out` | warning | 1 |  | An instance stands where `keep_out` is above 0; names the field and the position. |
| `place.margin_alone` | error | 1 |  | `margin` without `ground`. |
| `place.no_footprint` | error | 2 |  | `ground` on an asset with no footprint; only a model measures a point footprint, `assets.md` 2.4 (M2). |
| `place.no_position` | error | 1 |  | An instance or pin has neither `at` nor `on`; a run has no `on`. |
| `place.on_form` | error | 1 |  | `span` in an instance's `on`, or `t` in a run's `on`. (`t` or `offset` on a thing with no length is `geom.no_length`.) |
| `place.outside` | error | 1 |  | A hand instance or set item whose origin is outside the extent; not placed (8.4). |
| `place.overlap` | error | 1 |  | Two hand instances' footprints overlap on one level (8.1); names both. Two instances one step returned are `place.crowded`. |
| `place.range` | error | 1 |  | On an instance, run or set item: `scale` not above 0, `tint` below 0, `margin` below 0, or a `[lo, hi]` pair (only a scatter draws). |
| `place.relief` | warning | 1 |  | Relief under an instance exceeds its asset's `max_relief`; gives both numbers and the position. |

### `place.asset_or_set`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A placement writes both `asset` and `set`, or neither. It places one asset or one set. A run may
name a list of assets, one for each member, in place of either: it writes exactly one of `asset`,
`set` and `assets`.
To fix: Keep one of asset and set; on a run, one of asset, set and assets.
Bad:   [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       set = "c"
Fixed: [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
```

### `place.crowded`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
Two produced instances overlap, or one overlaps a thing in a higher layer, or two things one step
returned overlap: a member of its run and its instance, or two of its instances. A step wrote
both at once, so neither gives way. A warning: both stay. The record names both.
To fix: Change one producer's on or span, or add a clear or pin in the higher layer whose by names
the lower producer. For two things of one step, change what the step returns, or move one of the
things it was given (two calls of one step do not see each other's output).
Bad:   two runs along one path at the same offset
Fixed: on = { ref = "a", span = [0.1, 0.4], offset = 4 }   for one of them
```

### `place.gave_way`

info, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A producer's candidates were dropped because they overlapped hand instances or exceeded the
relief allowed. The record gives the counts and their box. Information only.
To fix: Nothing if intended; otherwise widen the space, or change the hand instances it gives way
to.
Bad:   a run of 20 posts where 8 give way to an instance
Fixed: the run's span moved clear of the instance
```

### `place.keep_out`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A hand instance stands where a keep_out field is above 0. It stays, since it is placed as
written; the record names the field and the position.
To fix: Move it, or change the kind whose effect writes keep_out there.
Bad:   [instance.a]  at = [10, 10]   (keep_out 1 there)
Fixed: [instance.a]  at = [30, 10]
```

### `place.margin_alone`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
`margin` is written without `ground`. margin is how far the ground footprint grows beyond the
asset's footprint; without ground there is no footprint feature to grow.
To fix: Add ground = "<kind>", or remove margin.
Bad:   [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       margin = 1
Fixed: [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       ground = "k"
       margin = 1
```

### `place.no_footprint`

error, milestone 2, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
ground on an asset with no footprint.
To fix: Declare the asset's footprint, or remove ground.
Bad:   asset = "lamp_post"   (no footprint)
       ground = "pad"
Fixed: the asset given a footprint, or `ground` removed
```

### `place.no_position`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
An instance or pin has neither at nor on, or a run has no on, so it has no place.
To fix: Write at or on (a run takes on).
Bad:   [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
Fixed: [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       at = [10, 10]
```

### `place.on_form`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
An instance's on holds span, or a run's on holds t. An instance stands at one point (t); a run
fills a stretch (span).
To fix: Write t on an instance, span on a run.
Bad:   [run.a]
       on = { ref = "b", t = 0.5 }
Fixed: [run.a]
       on = { ref = "b", span = [0.2, 0.8] }
```

### `place.outside`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A hand instance or set item has its origin outside the extent, so it is not placed.
To fix: Move it inside the extent, or widen the extent.
Bad:   at = [300, 10]   (extent [0, 0, 256, 256])
Fixed: at = [250, 10]
```

### `place.overlap`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
Two hand instances' footprints overlap on one level. Both are placed as written, so neither gives
way. The record names both and the overlap's size. Two instances that one step returned are not
two hands' decisions: their overlap is place.crowded, a warning.
To fix: Move one by at least the overlap's size.
Bad:   [instance.a] at = [10, 10]   and   [instance.b] at = [12, 10]   (each 4 m wide)
Fixed: [instance.b] at = [15, 10]
```

### `place.range`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
On an instance, run or set item: scale not above 0, tint below 0, margin below 0, or a [lo, hi]
pair, which only a scatter draws from.
To fix: Write a single value inside the key's range.
Bad:   scale = [0.8, 1.2]   (on an instance)
Fixed: scale = 1
```

### `place.relief`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
The ground under an instance varies more than its asset's max_relief allows. The record gives
both numbers and the position.
To fix: Move it, give it ground with a kind that levels, or choose an asset with a larger
max_relief.
Bad:   [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       at = [10, 10]
Fixed: [instance.a]
       asset = "b"
       at = [10, 10]
       ground = "k"   (k levels the ground)
```

## protocol

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol.absolute_path` | error | 1 |  | `command` holds an absolute path. |
| `protocol.blob_digest` | error | 2 |  | A blob's bytes do not match its name (M2). |
| `protocol.blob_header` | error | 2 |  | A column blob whose header or size does not match the `dtype` and `shape` its message gives. A non-finite sample is `num.not_finite_result` (4.2) (M2). |
| `protocol.code_folder` | error | 1 |  | The code folder is or holds the world's folder; move the script into its own folder. |
| `protocol.column_mixed` | error | 1 |  | One attribute has two types across the selected kinds; names both kinds. |
| `protocol.commit_refused` | error | 2 |  | `via step commit` found errors in the build; nothing written (M2). |
| `protocol.crashed` | error | 2 |  | The worker exited during a call (M2). |
| `protocol.deadline` | error | 1 | `phase`, `deadline` | No answer by the deadline; which phase, `data.phase` (`initialize`, `step.call` or `cancel`), and the deadline in seconds, `data.deadline`. |
| `protocol.explain_differs` | warning | 1 |  | A step sent two `explain` texts for one code. |
| `protocol.failed` | error | 1 | `exit` | A plain command exited non-zero; `data.exit`. |
| `protocol.field_file` | error | 2 |  | A returned field file is outside 4.2's `.npy` subset, or has the wrong `descr` or `shape` for its field; the hint is `step.out.field` (M2). |
| `protocol.for_each_form` | error | 2 |  | `for_each` is not `kind:<name>` (M2). |
| `protocol.framing` | error | 2 |  | A frame was not `Content-Length` and JSON; likely output written to the protocol descriptor (M2). |
| `protocol.input_undeclared` | error | 2 |  | `input.open` named a path not in `inputs` (M2). |
| `protocol.key_shadows` | error | 2 |  | A returned key equals a name the step can see (M2). |
| `protocol.message_too_large` | error | 2 | `bytes` | A frame over 16 MiB, `data.bytes` long; send the data as a blob (M2). |
| `protocol.no_entry` | error | 2 |  | The script has no top-level function named after `when` (M2). |
| `protocol.no_explain` | warning | 1 |  | A step sent a code with no `explain` text. |
| `protocol.no_output` | error | 2 |  | A generate step returned no document (M2). |
| `protocol.no_program` | error | 1 |  | `command[0]` is no configured program and no file, or is a `.bat`/`.cmd`; the hint gives `via config program`. |
| `protocol.output_file` | error | 2 |  | A returned `file` leaves `out` or names nothing (M2). |
| `protocol.output_json` | error | 1 |  | A plain command's `out/diagnostics.json` is not a list of diagnostic objects. |
| `protocol.output_table` | error | 1 |  | A returned document holds a table or key a step may not return, or a lint or export returned one. |
| `protocol.output_twice` | error | 2 |  | A worker returned a document and wrote `document.toml` (M2). |
| `protocol.raised` | error | 2 | `exception` | The step raised an exception it did not catch; `data.exception` (M2). |
| `protocol.slow_exit` | info | 2 |  | A worker had to be killed after `shutdown` (M2). |
| `protocol.start` | error | 1 | `kind` | The process could not be started; `data.kind` (6.2). |
| `protocol.unknown_library` | error | 1 | `nearest` | A `lib:` element names a library not in `include`; the nearest name. |
| `protocol.untrusted` | error | 2 |  | A generate step is not trusted and has no committed result; the hint is `via trust` (M2). |
| `protocol.untrusted_result` | info | 2 |  | An untrusted step was built from its committed result, which matched (M2). |
| `protocol.untrusted_skipped` | warning | 1 |  | An untrusted lint or export step was skipped. |
| `protocol.untrusted_stale` | error | 2 |  | A committed result's static key or a read of its trace differs from the current build; names the first difference (M2). |
| `protocol.version` | error | 2 | `engine`, `worker` | The worker speaks another protocol version; both versions, `data.engine` and `data.worker` (M2). |
| `protocol.when_unserved` | error | 2 | `when` | The worker's `capabilities.when` lacks the step's `when`, `data.when` (M2). |

### `protocol.absolute_path`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A step's command holds an absolute path, which would not exist on another machine.
To fix: Name a configured program, a path relative to the declaring document, or lib:<library>/.
Bad:   command = ["/usr/bin/python3", "a.py"]
Fixed: command = ["python", "steps/a.py"]
```

### `protocol.blob_digest`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A blob's bytes do not match its name.
To fix: A defect of the SDK or the transport: report it with the step.
Bad:   a blob named by one digest holding other bytes
Fixed: the blob written through the SDK, named by its own digest
```

### `protocol.blob_header`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A column blob whose header or size does not match the dtype and shape its message gives. A non-finite sample is num.not_finite_result (4.2).
To fix: Send the column through the SDK's column writer.
Bad:   {"dtype": "f4", "shape": [10]} over 36 bytes
Fixed: {"dtype": "f4", "shape": [9]} over 36 bytes
```

### `protocol.code_folder`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A step's code folder (the folder of its script) is, or holds, the world file's folder. Every edit
to the world would then change the step's trust digest and need trusting again.
To fix: Move the script into a folder of its own.
Bad:   command = ["python", "a.py"]   (a.py beside world.toml)
Fixed: command = ["python", "steps/a.py"]
```

### `protocol.column_mixed`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
One attribute has two types across the kinds a step selected (a number in one, a text in
another), so it cannot be one column. The record names both kinds.
To fix: Give the attribute one type in both kinds, or rename it in one.
Bad:   [kind.a]  defaults = { w = 1 }   and   [kind.b]  defaults = { w = "1" }
Fixed: [kind.b]  defaults = { w = 1 }
```

### `protocol.commit_refused`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
via step commit found errors in the build; nothing written (M2).
To fix: Fix the build's errors, then commit again.
Bad:   via step commit world.toml   (the build has an error)
Fixed: the error fixed, then via step commit world.toml
```

### `protocol.crashed`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The worker exited during a call.
To fix: Read the step's log in the run report; fix what ended the process.
Bad:   a worker that calls sys.exit() inside generate
Fixed: generate returns; errors are raised or sent as diagnostics
```

### `protocol.deadline`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A step gave no answer by its deadline. `data.phase` says which phase (initialize, step.call or
cancel) and `data.deadline` the deadline in seconds.
To fix: Make the step faster, or raise its deadline.
Bad:   a step that waits on the network at start
Fixed: the same step reading its data from a declared input
```

### `protocol.explain_differs`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A step sent two different explain texts for one code. via explain prints one, so the first is
kept.
To fix: Send one explain text per code, from one place in the step.
Bad:   two emits of code "a" with different explain strings
Fixed: one constant explain string for "a"
```

### `protocol.failed`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A plain command (a step that does not speak the protocol) exited non-zero. `data.exit` holds the
exit status.
To fix: Run the command by hand from the declaring document's folder and fix its error.
Bad:   command = ["python", "steps/a.py"]   (exits 1)
Fixed: the same command after fixing a.py
```

### `protocol.field_file`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A returned field file is outside 4.2's .npy subset, or has the wrong descr or shape for its field; the hint is step.out.field.
To fix: Write it with `step.out.field`.
Bad:   numpy.save("out/land.npy", land.astype("float64"))
Fixed: step.out.field("land", land)
```

### `protocol.for_each_form`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
for_each is not kind:<name> (M2).
To fix: Write `for_each = "kind:<name>"` on a generate step.
Bad:   for_each = "tarns"
Fixed: for_each = "kind:tarn"
```

### `protocol.framing`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A frame was not Content-Length and JSON; likely output written to the protocol descriptor.
To fix: Print to standard error, never to the protocol's output.
Bad:   print("done")   in a worker
Fixed: print("done", file=sys.stderr)
```

### `protocol.input_undeclared`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
input.open named a path not in inputs.
To fix: Add the path to the step's `inputs`.
Bad:   step.input("survey.png") with inputs = []
Fixed: inputs = ["survey.png"]
```

### `protocol.key_shadows`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A returned key equals a name the step can see.
To fix: Name the returned table other than the name it shadows.
Bad:   step.out.feature("pool", ...)   (a written feature `pool` is in its stratum)
Fixed: step.out.feature("found_pool", ...)
```

### `protocol.message_too_large`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A frame over 16 MiB; send the data as a blob.
To fix: Send the data as a blob (the SDK's columns do).
Bad:   one call carrying 40 MiB of JSON numbers
Fixed: the same values as an f4 column blob
```

### `protocol.no_entry`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The script has no top-level function named after when.
To fix: Define the function the step's `when` names.
Bad:   when = "generate", and the script defines only lint(step)
Fixed: def generate(step): ...
```

### `protocol.no_explain`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A step sent a code without explain text, so via explain has nothing to print for it.
To fix: Send explain with the first diagnostic of each code.
Bad:   step.diag.emit(code="a", subject="feature.b", message="m", hint="h")
Fixed: step.diag.emit(code="a", subject="feature.b", message="m", hint="h", explain="what a means")
```

### `protocol.no_output`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A generate step returned no document.
To fix: Return a document; an empty one when there is nothing to return.
Bad:   a generate step that writes nothing into out
Fixed: out/document.toml written, empty if need be (the SDK writes it)
```

### `protocol.no_program`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
command[0] is a name with no configured program and no file of that path, or is a .bat or .cmd
file, which is refused. Programs are never looked up on PATH.
To fix: Configure it: via config program <name> <path>.
Bad:   command = ["python3", "steps/a.py"]   (no program python3 configured)
Fixed: via config program python3 /usr/bin/python3
```

### `protocol.output_file`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A returned file leaves out or names nothing.
To fix: Write the file into `out` and name it relative to `out`.
Bad:   file = "/tmp/land.npy"
Fixed: file = "land.npy"
```

### `protocol.output_json`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A plain command's out/diagnostics.json is not a list of diagnostic objects.
To fix: Write a JSON list of objects with the diagnostic members (severity, code, subject,
message, hint).
Bad:   {"code": "a"}
Fixed: [{"severity": "warning", "code": "a", "subject": "feature.b", "message": "m", "hint": "h"}]
```

### `protocol.output_table`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A returned document holds a table or key a step may not return ([change], [kind], [let], remove,
unset), or a lint or export step returned a document at all.
To fix: Return only the tables the step's when allows; a lint or export returns diagnostics only.
Bad:   a generate step returning [kind.a]
Fixed: the step returning [feature.a] with kind = "a"
```

### `protocol.output_twice`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A worker returned a document and wrote document.toml.
To fix: Return the document one way.
Bad:   the call's result holds a document and out/document.toml is written
Fixed: only the SDK's step.out
```

### `protocol.raised`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The step raised an exception it did not catch; data.exception.
To fix: Read `data.exception`; fix the step, or catch and report what you mean to say.
Bad:   a step dividing by a zero area
Fixed: the case checked, sent as a diagnostic with a hint
```

### `protocol.slow_exit`

info, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A worker had to be killed after shutdown.
To fix: Return from the step promptly after `shutdown`; close threads and files.
Bad:   a worker that keeps a thread running after the build
Fixed: the thread joined before the step returns
```

### `protocol.start`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The step's process could not be started. `data.kind` says why: not_found, denied, other, or empty
for an empty command.
To fix: Check the program path and that it is executable.
Bad:   command = ["steps/a.sh"]   (not executable)
Fixed: command = ["sh", "steps/a.sh"]   (with sh configured)
```

### `protocol.unknown_library`

error, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A lib: element names a library that is not in the world's include. `data.nearest` holds the
nearest included library.
To fix: Write an included library, or add it to include.
Bad:   command = ["python", "lib:chcks/a.py"]
Fixed: command = ["python", "lib:checks/a.py"]
```

### `protocol.untrusted`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A generate step is not trusted and has no committed result; the hint is via trust.
To fix: Read the step's code folder, then run `via trust WORLD`.
Bad:   via build world.toml   (the step never trusted on this machine)
Fixed: via trust world.toml, then via build world.toml
```

### `protocol.untrusted_result`

info, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
An untrusted step was built from its committed result, which matched (M2).
To fix: None needed; trust the step to run it here.
Bad:   (nothing wrong) a committed result used for an untrusted step
Fixed: via trust world.toml, to run the step instead
```

### `protocol.untrusted_skipped`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A lint or export step is not trusted, so it was skipped. The build is complete without it.
To fix: Review the step and trust it with via trust.
Bad:   via build world.toml   (step not in trust.toml)
Fixed: via trust world.toml, then via build world.toml
```

### `protocol.untrusted_stale`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
A committed result's static key or a read of its trace differs from the current build; names the first difference (M2).
To fix: Trust the step and build, or commit a new result from a trusted build.
Bad:   gen/terrain/ committed before a fact it read moved
Fixed: via trust world.toml; via build; via step commit world.toml
```

### `protocol.version`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The worker speaks another protocol version; both versions.
To fix: Use the SDK carried with this engine.
Bad:   an SDK of another protocol version on the path
Fixed: python -m viasdk with the engine's own SDK first on PYTHONPATH
```

### `protocol.when_unserved`

error, milestone 2, `spec/protocol.md`.

```text
The worker's capabilities.when lacks the step's when.
To fix: Serve the step's `when` from the program, or change `when`.
Bad:   when = "lint" on a program that serves only generate
Fixed: when = "generate"
```

## run

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run.count` | error | 3 |  | `count` below 1, or below 2 with `ends = "both"` on an open stretch; `assets` empty, or too short for its `ends`; or `count` beside `assets` that is not the list's length, with both numbers (M3). |
| `run.count_or_spacing` | error | 3 |  | A run writes both `count` and `spacing`, or neither; or `spacing` beside `assets` (M3). |
| `run.no_length` | error | 3 |  | The run's `on` names a thing with no length, or its stretch is zero millimetres (M3). |
| `run.outside` | warning | 3 |  | Members fell outside the extent and were not made; gives the count (M3). |

### `run.count`

error, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
count below 1, or below 2 with ends = "both" on an open stretch. On a run with assets, whose list
is the count: the list is empty or too short for its ends, or count is written beside it and is
not the list's length (the record gives both numbers).
To fix: The least allowed count. Beside assets, the list's length, or no count.
Bad:   count = 1, ends = "both"   (on a path)
Fixed: count = 2, ends = "both"
```

### `run.count_or_spacing`

error, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A run writes both count and spacing, or neither. Or it writes spacing beside assets: a run with
assets has one member for each entry of the list, so the list is the count.
To fix: Keep one. With assets, drop spacing; a count there must equal the list's length (run.count).
Bad:   count = 4, spacing = 3
Fixed: count = 4
```

### `run.no_length`

error, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
The run's on names a thing with no length, or its stretch is zero millimetres.
To fix: Name a path or region, or widen span.
Bad:   on = { ref = "well" }   (a point feature)
Fixed: on = { ref = "edge", span = [0, 0.5] }
```

### `run.outside`

warning, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
Members fell outside the extent and were not made; gives the count.
To fix: Narrow span to the part inside the extent.
Bad:   on = { ref = "edge", span = [0, 1] }   (the path runs past the extent)
Fixed: on = { ref = "edge", span = [0, 0.4] }
```

## scatter

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scatter.clump` | error | 2 |  | `clump` breaks 7.3: both forms, no `radius`, a value out of range, or `around` naming a non-producer (M2). |
| `scatter.empty` | warning | 1 |  | A scatter placed nothing; names the stage that removed the last candidate. |
| `scatter.keep_out_twice` | info | 1 |  | `density` reads a `keep_out` field, which the scatter already applies. |
| `scatter.range` | error | 1 |  | A `[lo, hi]` with `lo > hi`, a `scale` not above 0, a `tint` below 0, a `jitter` outside 0 to 1, a `spacing` not above 0, or a `weight` not above 0. |
| `scatter.within` | error | 1 |  | `within` names a path or a point. |

### `scatter.clump`

error, milestone 2, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
clump breaks 7.3: both forms, no radius, a value out of range, or around naming a non-producer.
To fix: The key to remove or change.
Bad:   clump = { members = [2, 5] }   (no radius)
Fixed: clump = { members = [2, 5], radius = 6.5 }
```

### `scatter.empty`

warning, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A scatter placed nothing. The record names the stage that removed the last candidate (density,
within, keep_out, a hand edit).
To fix: Change the key behind that stage.
Bad:   density = "= if(f('height') > 90, 0.6, 0)"   (height never above 90)
Fixed: density = 0.6
```

### `scatter.keep_out_twice`

info, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
`density` reads a keep_out field, which the scatter already applies to every candidate, so it is
counted twice.
To fix: Remove the keep_out factor from density.
Bad:   density = "= 0.6 * (1 - f('b'))"   (b has role keep_out)
Fixed: density = 0.6
```

### `scatter.range`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A scatter key is out of range: a [lo, hi] with lo > hi, a scale not above 0, a tint below 0, a
jitter outside 0 to 1, a spacing not above 0, or a weight not above 0.
To fix: Write the key inside its range.
Bad:   scale = [1.2, 0.8]
Fixed: scale = [0.8, 1.2]
```

### `scatter.within`

error, milestone 1, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
`within` names a path or a point, which has no inside to scatter in.
To fix: Name a region feature, a footprint feature, or select an area, cell, rest or piece.
Bad:   within = "a"   (a is a path)
Fixed: within = "b"   (b is a region)
```

## set

| Code | Severity | M | Data | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set.empty` | error | 3 |  | A set has no items (M3). |
| `set.unknown` | error | 3 | `nearest` | `set` names no set (M3). |
| `set.unused` | info | 3 |  | A set nothing places (M3). |

### `set.empty`

error, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A set has no items.
To fix: Add [set.<id>.item.<name>], or remove the set.
Bad:   [set.pair]   (no item)
Fixed: [set.pair.item.l] asset = "lamp_post"
```

### `set.unknown`

error, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
set names no set.
To fix: The nearest set id.
Bad:   set = "lamp_pair"
Fixed: set = "lamp_pairs"
```

### `set.unused`

info, milestone 3, `spec/rules.md`.

```text
A set nothing places.
To fix: Place it with an instance or run, or remove it.
Bad:   [set.lamp_pair.item.l] ...   (no instance or run names lamp_pair)
Fixed: [instance.front_lamps] set = "lamp_pair", on = { ref = "cottage.front" }
```
