| `surface.meets_twice` | error | 3 |  | The mount is in two `meets` pairs; names both others. |
| `surface.mount_face` | error | 3 |  | A face word on a kind mount. Hint: a number, 0 along travel, 180 against. |
| `surface.name_clash` | error | 3 |  | A surface and a mount share a name. |
| `surface.none_at` | error | 5 |  | Its `at` carries a height, and no kind surface's bound holds the plan point (4.1). Hint: drop the third number to stand on the terrain, or move it onto a surface. |
| `surface.not_surface` | error | 5 |  | Its `surface` names a place that is not a kind surface (a mount, a feature, the terrain's field); lists the owner's surfaces. |
| `surface.off_bound` | warning | 3 |  | Part of its footprint lies outside its surface's bound; the share. |
| `surface.on_rise` | error | 7 |  | Its `on` names an asset mount with a `rise`: nothing stands there (3.2). Names the mount and its rise. |
| `surface.outside` | error | 3 |  | Its plan point lies inside the extent but outside the bound of the kind surface it stands on. An origin outside the extent is `place.outside` (`rules.md` 8.4), never this code. |
| `surface.owner_shape` | error | 3 |  | A surface on a point kind, a path owner without `bound`, or a region owner with one. |
| `surface.placed_twice` | error | 5 |  | `surface` written with `on`, or with a height in `at`: each already says the surface. Hint: drop `surface`, or place it by `at` with two numbers. |
| `surface.through` | warning | 3 |  | Its height reaches through another surface above its origin; names it. |
| `surface.too_early` | error | 2 |  | `meetings()` called at `generate`. |
| `surface.two_terrains` | error | 1 |  | Two surface fields at the top level. Hint: make one a kind's surface. |
| `surface.unknown_mount` | error | 3 |  | `meets` names a mount the kind lacks; lists the kind's mounts. |
| `surface.unknown_surface` | error | 3 |  | `surface` names a surface the kind lacks; lists the kind's surfaces. |
| `surface.unmet` | warning | 5 | `nearest` | A mount with a connector is answered by nothing (R18: a stub). Hint: "end a path whose kind has connector <c> here: `ends_at = \"<place>\"`". For an asset mount, also the nearest open mount of another instance with the same connector within 2 m, and the miss in millimetres (`near`, `miss`, `miss_z`), and the other instances' mounts at its own point (`beside`). |
| `surface.which` | error | 3 |  | `on` a thing, or a path end on a kind, with two or more surfaces; lists them. Hint: place it `on` a mount. |

### `surface.apart`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Two paired mounts lie at different plan points; gives both.
To fix: Put both mounts at one plan point: the same `t` and `offset`, or meet with another mount.
Bad:   [kind.span.mount.a] t = 0, and [kind.span.mount.b] t = 0.1, meets = "a"
Fixed: [kind.span.mount.b] t = 0, meets = "a"
```

### `surface.bound`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Its bound is not above 0 or not finite; gives the value.
To fix: Give `bound` a value above 0 for every owner, through the kind's defaults or the feature's attributes.
Bad:   bound = "= width / 2"   (with width = 0)
Fixed: bound = "= max(width, 0.5) / 2"
```

### `surface.clipped`

info, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Its bound reaches beyond the extent; the share lost.
To fix: Nothing if the bound may reach past the edge; otherwise move the owner inside, or widen the extent.
Bad:   a path owner's surface bound running 3 m past the east edge
Fixed: the owner's path ending 3 m inside the extent
```

### `surface.connector`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Two sides of a meeting both carry a connector, and the words differ: a path end takes its kind's
connector, a mount its own. Connectors are free words compared only for equality, so a joint meets
only a joint of the same word.
To fix: End a path of the matching kind there, or change one side's connector.
Bad:   a path of a kind with connector = "rail" ending at a mount with connector = "way"
Fixed: a path of a kind with connector = "way" ending there
```

### `surface.cut`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A kind surface's cut, the height above the surface in which the terrain's export is removed, came
out below 0 or not finite for this feature.
To fix: Make the cut formula give 0 or more; leave cut out for no cut.
Bad:   cut = "= clear_h" with clear_h = -1
Fixed: clear_h = 2.6
```

### `surface.empty_region`

error, milestone 1, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A region whose relief was asked (how much the ground varies under it) has zero area, so there
is nothing to measure.
To fix: Ask with a region that has area: its points must not all lie on one line.
Bad:   relief asked for [[0, 0], [10, 0], [20, 0]]
Fixed: relief asked for [[0, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10]]
```

### `surface.facing`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Two mounts paired by meets, or two instances' mounts that join at one point, both have a face,
and their world bearings are not half a turn apart: one should look into the joint and the other
out of it.
To fix: Set one face 180 degrees from the other; 0 looks along travel, 180 against it. For two
instances, turn one of them.
Bad:   [kind.span.mount.end_top] face = 0 and [kind.span.mount.end_low] face = 0, paired by meets
Fixed: end_low face = 180
```

### `surface.fold`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Its strip overlaps itself; position and the largest bound that holds.
To fix: Widen the bend or narrow the bound to the largest that holds, which the record gives.
Bad:   a path owner with width = 5 on a bend of inner radius 1 m
Fixed: width = 1.8, or a bend of radius 3 m
```

### `surface.gap`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
The two sides differ in height; both heights, the gap in millimetres, and what sets each (3.4). Hint: "make the two sides equal: change <a> or <b>, or add an effect of <owner> that sets the ground to <z>".
To fix: Make the two sides equal: change one side's height, or add an effect of the owner that sets the ground to the surface's height there.
Bad:   a surface at top_z and no effect raising the ground at its ends
Fixed: add [kind.span.effect.heads] with value = "= top_z" at each end
```

### `surface.ground_off_terrain`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
ground on an instance that stands on a kind surface.
To fix: Remove `ground`, or stand the instance on the terrain.
Bad:   on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 1 }, ground = "level"
Fixed: on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 1 }
```

### `surface.host_missing`

error, milestone 1, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A thing is placed on something, or on a mount of something, that was not placed (it failed, or
was removed), so it has no surface to stand on.
To fix: Fix why the host was not placed, or place this thing elsewhere.
Bad:   on = { ref = "a.m" }   (instance a outside the extent)
Fixed: on = { ref = "a.m" }   with a moved inside the extent
```

### `surface.joint_many`

error, milestone 7, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Two instances' mounts that each have a connector and lie at one plan point answer each other: a
joint, with nothing written for it. Here three or more such mounts, not all of one instance, lie
at one point and one height, so each would be in two joints. None is joined. They are named
here and not also reported as unanswered.
To fix: Move all but two of the pieces away, or take the connector off the mounts that join nothing.
Bad:   three pipe pieces whose end mounts all lie at [40, 40], 5 m up
Fixed: two pieces end there; the third ends one piece further on
```

### `surface.meets_self`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
meets names the mount itself.
To fix: Name another mount of the same kind in `meets`, or remove `meets`.
Bad:   [kind.span.mount.west_top] meets = "west_top"
Fixed: [kind.span.mount.west_top] meets = "west_head"
```

### `surface.meets_twice`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
The mount is in two meets pairs; names both others.
To fix: Keep one pair for the mount: remove `meets` from one of the two others.
Bad:   [kind.span.mount.a] meets = "c", and [kind.span.mount.b] meets = "c"
Fixed: [kind.span.mount.b] meets = "d"
```

### `surface.mount_face`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A face word on a kind mount. Hint: a number, 0 along travel, 180 against.
To fix: Write a number of degrees: 0 along travel, 180 against.
Bad:   face = "along"
Fixed: face = 0
```

### `surface.name_clash`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A surface and a mount share a name.
To fix: Rename the surface or the mount.
Bad:   [kind.span.surface.top] and [kind.span.mount.top]
Fixed: [kind.span.surface.top] and [kind.span.mount.top_west]
```

### `surface.none_at`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A placement's at has three numbers. The third is a height that chooses which kind surface at that
point the thing stands on, the one whose height there is nearest. Here no kind surface that its
layer sees holds the point, so there is nothing to choose from. The terrain is never chosen this
way: two numbers mean the terrain.
To fix: Drop the third number to stand on the terrain, or move the point onto a surface.
Bad:   at = [40, 40, 13.3]   (no surface there)
Fixed: at = [40, 40]   or   at = [30, 26, 13.3]
```

### `surface.not_surface`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
The surface key on a placement names a place, but not a kind surface: a mount, a path end, a
feature or the terrain's field. The terrain is the default and is never named.
To fix: Name <feature>.<surface>, one of the listed surfaces, or drop surface to stand on the terrain.
Bad:   surface = "hall.entry"   (a mount)
Fixed: surface = "hall.top"
```

### `surface.off_bound`

warning, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Part of its footprint lies outside its surface's bound; the share.
To fix: Move the instance so its footprint lies on the surface, or widen the surface's bound.
Bad:   on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 2 }   (half the footprint off the 5 m surface)
Fixed: on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 0 }
```

### `surface.on_rise`

error, milestone 7, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A thing placed on a mount stands on the surface that mount lies on. An asset mount with a rise
stands above the surface its instance stands on, and lies on none: there is nothing there to
stand on. A path may end at such a mount, and another instance's mount may join it.
To fix: Place the thing on a mount with no rise, or at a point, and give its own asset the mount
that joins this one.
Bad:   [instance.valve] on = { ref = "tank.outlet" }   (outlet has rise = 5)
Fixed: [instance.valve] at = [40, 42], with a mount of its own at the outlet's point and height
```

### `surface.outside`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Its plan point lies inside the extent but outside the bound of the kind surface it stands on. An origin outside the extent is place.outside (rules.md 8.4), never this code.
To fix: Move it onto the surface's bound, or onto the ground beside it.
Bad:   on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 4 }   (the surface is 2.5 m to each side)
Fixed: on = { ref = "span_a", t = 0.5, offset = 1 }
```

### `surface.owner_shape`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A surface on a point kind, a path owner without bound, or a region owner with one.
To fix: Give a path owner a `bound`, remove it from a region owner, or give the surface to a path or region kind.
Bad:   [kind.span.surface.top] base = ...   (no bound, on a path owner)
Fixed: [kind.span.surface.top] base = ..., bound = "= width / 2"
```

### `surface.placed_twice`

error, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A placement says twice what it stands on: surface written with on, or with a height as the third
number of at. On already decides it (the surface of the thing or mount it is on), and so does a
height (the surface nearest it), so the two could disagree.
To fix: Drop surface, or place it by at with two numbers and surface.
Bad:   on = { ref = "hall", t = 0.5 } and surface = "hall.top"
Fixed: at = [30, 26] and surface = "hall.top"
```

### `surface.through`

warning, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Its height reaches through another surface above its origin; names it.
To fix: Move it, or choose a lower asset; nothing if it really stands under the other surface.
Bad:   a 6 m mast under a surface 4.5 m above the ground
Fixed: the mast moved 6 m off the surface's line
```

### `surface.too_early`

error, milestone 2, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
meetings() called at generate.
To fix: Call meetings() from a lint step, which reads the finished build.
Bad:   step.meetings() inside generate(step)
Fixed: step.meetings() inside lint(step)
```

### `surface.two_terrains`

error, milestone 1, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
Two fields at the top level have role surface. A world has one terrain; other surfaces belong to
kinds.
To fix: Remove role from one, or make it a kind's surface.
Bad:   [field.a]  role = "surface"   and   [field.b]  role = "surface"
Fixed: [field.a]  role = "surface"   and   [field.b]  base = "= f('a') + 2"
```

### `surface.unknown_mount`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
meets names a mount the kind lacks; lists the kind's mounts.
To fix: Name a mount the kind declares; the record lists them.
Bad:   meets = "east_hed"
Fixed: meets = "east_head"
```

### `surface.unknown_surface`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
surface names a surface the kind lacks; lists the kind's surfaces.
To fix: Name a surface the kind declares; the record lists them.
Bad:   surface = "tpo"
Fixed: surface = "top"
```

### `surface.unmet`

warning, milestone 5, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
A kind or asset mount with a connector is the place of no path end and meets no mount with the
same connector: a joint left open. A meets pair whose other side has no connector does not count.
Path ends are never checked: a path end may be left free on purpose. For an asset mount it also
names the nearest open mount of another instance with the same connector within 2 m, and how far
the two miss in plan and in height: two instances' mounts at one point answer each other.
Where other instances' mounts lie at its own point (a third piece, a piece of another connector)
it lists them.
To fix: End a path whose kind has the same connector there, bring the two mounts it names to one
point and height, or remove the connector.
Bad:   an instance whose asset mount entry has connector = "foot", and no path ends at it
Fixed: [feature.walk] with ends_at = "<instance>.entry" and a kind with connector = "foot"
```

### `surface.which`

error, milestone 3, `spec/surfaces.md`.

```text
on a thing, or a path end on a kind, with two or more surfaces; lists them. Hint: place it on a mount.
To fix: Place it on one of the owner's mounts, which says the surface.
Bad:   on = { ref = "hall" }   (hall owns upper and lower)
Fixed: on = { ref = "hall.upper_mid" }
```
